title: Celery chain occasionally loses next task, breaking the chain
body:
# Checklist

- [ ] I have verified that the issue exists against the `main` branch of Celery.
- [ ] This has already been asked to the [discussions forum](https://github.com/celery/celery/discussions) first.
- [ ] I have read the relevant section in the
  [contribution guide](https://docs.celeryq.dev/en/main/contributing.html#other-bugs)
  on reporting bugs.
- [ ] I have checked the [issues list](https://github.com/celery/celery/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3A%22Issue+Type%3A+Bug+Report%22+-label%3A%22Category%3A+Documentation%22)
  for similar or identical bug reports.
- [ ] I have checked the [pull requests list](https://github.com/celery/celery/pulls?q=is%3Apr+label%3A%22PR+Type%3A+Bugfix%22+-label%3A%22Category%3A+Documentation%22)
  for existing proposed fixes.
- [ ] I have checked the [commit log](https://github.com/celery/celery/commits/main)
  to find out if the bug was already fixed in the main branch.
- [ ] I have included all related issues and possible duplicate issues
  in this issue (If there are none, check this box anyway).
- [ ] I have tried to reproduce the issue with [pytest-celery](https://docs.celeryq.dev/projects/pytest-celery/en/latest/userguide/celery-bug-report.html) and added the reproduction script below.

## Mandatory Debugging Information

- [ ] I have included the output of ``celery -A proj report`` in the issue.
    (if you are not able to do this, then at least specify the Celery
    version affected).
- [ ] I have verified that the issue exists against the `main` branch of Celery.
- [ ] I have included the contents of ``pip freeze`` in the issue.
- [ ] I have included all the versions of all the external dependencies required
  to reproduce this bug.

## Environment & Settings

**Celery version**: [please specify]
**Python version**: [please specify]
Broker: RabbitMQ
Backend: Redis
Relevant config: `task_track_started`, `task_acks_late`, `task_acks_on_failure_or_timeout`, `task_reject_on_worker_lost`, `worker_prefetch_multiplier=1`, `result_persistent=True`

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Use `chain` to wrap several tasks and execute them.
2. Occasionally, the chain children become empty or the downstream task is not scheduled.

## Minimally Reproducible Test Case

```python
# Minimal test case:
# chain(task1.s(), task2.s(), task3.s()).apply_async()
# Occasionally, task2 and/or task3 do not execute, despite task1 completion.
```

## Expected Behavior

All tasks in the chain should execute sequentially and reliably. The chain should never break.

## Actual Behavior

Occasionally, chain children is empty, or the next task is not triggered, causing the chain to break.
Logs confirm that the head task completes, but subsequent tasks are not triggered.
Task arguments are guaranteed to be serializable and not oversized.
Both RabbitMQ and Redis are highly available, with no single points of failure.

## Questions

- Are there any known bugs related to chain losing the next task or breaking unexpectedly?
- Any recommendations for further debugging or investigation?
